Appellant has filed this appeal U/s. 29 of The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act,
2005( in short PWDV Act) praying to set aside the order dated 9.06.2023 passed by II MMTC Bangalore in Cri Misc No. 05/2023.

2 to 6 in the petition by carrying amendment.

(3) The respondents entered appearance by Cri Appeal No.1309/2023 engaging their counsel.

(5) In the memorandum of appeal, the appellant by reiterating the contents of petition filed U/s 12 of PWDV Act would contend that the respondent no 2 to 6 tortured her physically and mentally and committed domestic violence.
The definition shared household as defined U/s 2 (s) attracts to the present case.
The finding given by learned MMTC II Bangalore that respondent no. 2 to 6 are not residing in the shared household and dismissing the petition against respondent no. 2 to 6 is incorrect.
Hence on these among other grounds she prayed to set aside the impugned order dated 9.06.2023 in Criminal Misc No. 05/2023 passed by Learned MMTC II Bangalore.

monetary relief U/s 20 and to grant compensation and legal expenses U/s 22 of PWDV Act.

After such arranged marriage dated 21.02.2021, for few months appellant and respondent no. 1 stayed in matrimonial house.
It is alleged that respondent no. 2 started throwing taunts and hurling abuses.

she has not stated the actual job she carried prior to her marriage and after her marriage.
Even in the written arguments submitted by learned counsel for the appellant,it is not stated the nature of job of the appellant.

In the written Cri Appeal No.1309/2023 arguments filed by learned counsel for the respondents in para no. 4, it is submitted that appellant is well educated, financially independent individual working in a bank.

The reason this court noted this point is because,
according to the appellant, after her marriage with respondent no. 1 registered on 27.10.2020, upon demands of respondents, grand ceremony took place before their friends and family on 21.02.2021.

For that reason appellant and respondent no 1 went to the native place of respondent no. 1 i.e.,
village Kumhai, Chas, Bokaro, West Bengal.
The appellant/ petitioner in her petition filed U/s 12 of PWDV Act mentioned the same address of all the respondent no. 1 to 6.
Thus one thing to be noted here is that respondent no. 2 to 6 are not at all residing in Bangalore.
It was appellant and respondent no. 1 who were residing in Bangalore for their job even prior to their arranged marriage performed on 21.02.2021.

it is not the case of the appellant/ petitioner is that soon after the marriage registered on 27.10.2020, she along with respondent no. 1 went to the residence of respondent no. 2 to 6 situated at Bokaro.
Appellant and respondent no. 1 went to Bokaro inorder for performance of marriage on 21.02.2021.
The appellant Cri Appeal No.1309/2023 would contend that after the marriage, few months, she and respondent no. 1 stayed along with remaining respondents in matrimonial house.

On the other hand the learned counsel for the respondents in her written arguments stated that appellant stayed in her matrimonial house approximately 15 days in total during the marriage ceremonies which includes rituals, social gathering which took place in February 2021 and thereafter 3 years later during Durga pooja festival for few days, except these days at no other point of time appellant came to matrimonial home.

There is some force in the arguments of the learned counsel for the respondents, because if at all the appellant had stayed in the matrimonial home for few months after celebration of marriage on 21.2.2021, she would have specifically stated in the petition regarding how many days she had taken leave inorder to perform her marriage ceremonies and on which date she came back to Bangalore and start working from her office.

First of all there is no averments made in the petition regarding what was the actual job of the appellant in Bangalore whether it is in bank, company, firm, financial institution or Government departments.
In para no. 8 of her petition, she has stated Cri Appeal No.1309/2023 that her inlaws have been covetous of her wealth and earnings.
That indicates she had very good earning from her job in the Bangalore.
She further stated that she had extended financial support to her husband.
She is also financially helping her brother and sister.
All these averments made in the petition would indicate that she's having good job in Bangalore.
She has also stated that during the pandemic, in the month of September 2022, she had worked from home .

sentences.text: In the absence of any such averments made in her petition would go to show that she cleverly drafted the petition and filed affidavit only inorder to add the respondent no. 2 to 6 in this petition.
(12) The learned counsel for the appellant argued that the provision U/s 2(s) is very clear that the shared household means where the aggrieved person lives or lived at any stage.

There is no dispute regarding the definition of shared house household means where the person aggrieved lives or at any stage lived in a domestic Cri Appeal No.1309/2023 relationship, whether she got any right, title,
interest or equity over shared household or not.

But in the present case, when it is the specific case of the appellant is that only for the purpose of her marriage, she went to matrimonial home from Bangalore where she is working, she should have specifically stated from which date till which date she lived in matrimonial home at Bokaro.

On perusal of her affidavit filed in support of petition filed U/s 12 of PWDV Act from para no. 15 to para no. 27, she has narrated the date wise incident, gist of which is already mentioned by this court in afore said para.

When she could narrate the date wise incident which occurred from the month of September 2022, she should have atleast stated from which date or month till which date or month she has stayed in matrimonial home along with respondent no. 2 to Respondent no 6.
(13) On perusal of the entire petition averments filed U/s 12 of PWDV Act, there is no allegation made against respondent no. 5 and 6 I have already mentioned the gist of the petition averments.

There is absolutely no allegations made against respondent no 5 and 6 to attract Section 2(s) of PWDV Act to say that they were in a shared household Cri Appeal No.1309/2023 and that they have made domestic violence against the appellant.
Respondent no. 4 is no more.
The learned counsel for the respondents produced copy of death certificate of respondent no. 4 to show that he died on 23.02.2024.
The allegations made against respondent no. 2 to 4 are in the form of omnibus statements.
Respondent no. 2 and 3 have not resided along with appellant and respondent no. 1 at Bangalore.

The learned Counsel for the respondents produced the certificate copy of order passed by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Criminal Petition no. 6077 of 2024 wherein the Hon'ble High Court while staying the proceedings against Respondent 2, 3,5, and 6 in CC No. 8219/2023 pending on the file of XXXIX ACMM Bangalore for the offenses punishable U/s 498A, 506 R/w 34 of IPC and U/s 3 and 4 of DP Act

observed that on perusal of complaint or summary of the chargesheet in column no. 17, it would not indicate any allegation against these petitioner(Accused) that would touch upon the ingredients of the afore said offences.
Only omnibus statements on the sprinkling allegations are made against the petitioners.

Therefore permitting further proceeding to continue against the petitioners would run foul of the Cri Appeal No.1309/2023 judgment of the Apex Court in the case Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam and others V. State of Bihar and ors reported in 2022 SCC Online 162.

sentences.text: another version, she claimed that she and respondent no. 1 returned to Bangalore together as they were working in Bangalore.
The learned counsel for the appellant rightly pointed out these contradicted version of the appellant in this appeal and her original petition filed U/s 12 PWDV Act.
I have gone through the decisions cited by the learned counsel for the respondents in Preethi Guptas case, Kans raj case, U Suvetha's case, Geetha Mehrotra's case and Arnesh Kumar's case.
In my humble view, the principles laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in all these cited Cri Appeal No.1309/2023 decisions are applicable to the present case.

The learned counsel for the appellant relied on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court between Prabha Tyagi V. Kamblesh Devi reported in (2022) 8 SCC 90 wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that the expression "domestic Relationship" is a comprehensive one.

entities.text: Prabha Tyagi V. Kamblesh Devi reported in (2022) 8 SCC 90
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no dispute regarding the principles laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in this cited decision.
No doubt it is not necessary that at the time of filing of an application by an aggrieved person the domestic relationship should be subsisting.

In other words, even if an aggrieved person is not in a domestic relationship with the respondent in a shared household at the time of filing of an application U/s 12 of DV Act but has at any point of time lived so or had to right to live and has been subjected to domestic violence or is later subjected to domestic violence, on account of the domestic relationship is entitled to file an application U/s 12 of the DV Act as observed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in para no. 75.3 of this cited decision.
In the present case, as I already noted, there is absolutely no allegations made against respondent no. 5 and 6 to say that they have committed the domestic violence to the appellant.
The allegation made Cri Appeal No.1309/2023 against respondent no. 2 and 3 are in the form of omnibus statement.
As I already noted, the petitioner has not stated from which date she was in matrimonial home i.e., in the house of the respondents mentioned in the cause title.

As appellant went to the matrimonial house for specific purpose of celebration of her marriage with respondent no. 1, it cannot be held that the respondent no. 2 to 6 are residing in the same shared house along with the appellant and respondent no.1.

It is not the case of the appellant is that at any any point of time, respondent no. 2,
3, 5 and 6 came to Bangalore and stayed in the shared house of appellant and respondent no.1 .

Since the appellant is working in Bangalore, she should have stated in petition how many days she had taken leave for her marriage and from which date to which date she had been to the house of respondent no. 2 to 6 for celebration of her marriage and on which date she returned to Bangalore and started to work at Bangalore.
In absence of all these averments, mere using the word few months she started at matrimonial house is not suffice to hold that respondent no. 2 to 6 are residing in the same shared household.
At one stretch the petitioner in her petition would contend that while she was Cri Appeal No.1309/2023 staying at the matrimonial house, respondents subjected her to domestic violence.
But in another stretch she would contend that in the moth of march 2022, she went along with her husband respondent no. 1 on trip for wedding anniversary.

She has not stated to which place they went to celebrate wedding anniversary but learned counsel for the respondents in the written arguments submitted that appellant and respondent no. 1 went on honeymoon to Maldives and enjoyed a peaceful and harmonious relationship during that time.
This contradicts her claim of ill treatment.
If at all the respondent no. 2 to 6 have give her mental torture or made abuse in any manner and instigating respondent no. 1
, there was no such chance to go on such trip in the month of March 2022.
The reason the court noted down this is because the main allegation of the appellant against respondent no. 2 to 6 is that they have given domestic violence in matrimonial home.
The learned MMTC II rightly held that there is no specific allegation against respondent no. 2 to 6 except verbal abuse and instigation to the respondent no. 1.

Even respondent Dipa Kayal Dutta vs Rakesh Kumar Dutta on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177530437/
7 no. 2 to 6 are not residing in the same shared household.

sentences.text: The learned magistrate rightly dismissed the Cri Appeal No.1309/2023 petition against respondent no. 2 to 6.
There is no illegality in the impugned order.
The learned MMTC II after perusal of the petition averments and material available on record rightly dismissed the petition against respondent no. 2 to 6.
There is no sufficient grounds made out by the appellant to set aside order dated 9.06.2023 passed by MMTC II Bangalore in Criminal Misc. No. 5/2023.
hence I answered point no 1 in the negative (15) Point No. 2:-
In the result I proceed to pass the following :-
ORDER The appeal filed by the appellant U/s 29 of PWDV Act 2005 R/w Section 381 of Cr.P.C is hereby Dismissed.
The order dated 9.06.2023 in Cri Misc no. 05/2023 passed by learned MMTC II Bangalore is hereby confirmed.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In other words, even if an aggrieved person is not in a domestic relationship with the respondent in a shared household at the time of filing of an application U/s 12 of DV Act but has at any point of time lived so or had to right to live and has been subjected to domestic violence or is later subjected to domestic violence, on account of the domestic relationship is entitled to file an application U/s 12 of the DV Act as observed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in para no. 75.3 of this cited decision.
As appellant went to the matrimonial house for specific purpose of celebration of her marriage with respondent no. 1, it cannot be held that the respondent no. 2 to 6 are residing in the same shared house along with the appellant and respondent no.1.
In absence of all these averments, mere using the word few months she started at matrimonial house is not suffice to hold that respondent no. 2 to 6 are residing in the same shared household.
, there was no such chance to go on such trip in the month of March 2022.
Even respondent Dipa Kayal Dutta vs Rakesh Kumar Dutta on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177530437/
7 no. 2 to 6 are not residing in the same shared household.
The learned magistrate rightly dismissed the Cri Appeal No.1309/2023 petition against respondent no. 2 to 6.
There is no illegality in the impugned order.
